To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) pigeons can produce and exchange tokens for food and water in a token economy; (2) the number of tokens produced increases as the exchange schedule is increased; (3) pigeons produce more generalized than specific food tokens under a water restricted budget; (4) pigeons produce fewer generalized than specific food or water tokens under a food restricted budget; (5) production of each token type declines as a function of own-price, and increases as a function of cross-price; and

pigeons in a simulated token economy produced more generalized than food or water specific tokens and that the number of tokens produced was a function of their own and the other token type's price, and that these effects were consistent across conditions of water and food restriction.

pigeons produced more tokens when their exchange-production schedule was higher and that the number of tokens produced under water restriction increased when the exchange-production schedule for generalized tokens was increased, suggesting that the reinforcing efficacy of tokens can be generalized across commodities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of economic contingencies on the production and exchange of generalized tokens.
the development of an animal model for studying the effects of economic contingencies on human behavior in a token economy.
the generalization of conditioned reinforcement in pigeons.

the results are interesting and suggest the possibility of a new approach to the study of economic behavior.
the results of these experiments are consistent with economic theory, and that they suggest a promising method for studying economic principles in animals in the laboratory.
the results of this research are consistent with the notion that generalized conditioned reinforcement with pigeions is possible and that the method is useful for the study of economic behavior.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

generalized conditioned reinforcement can be demonstrated with pigeons in the token economy, and that the generalized functions of tokens are sensitive to economic contingencies. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2016 APA, all rights reserved)
generalized tokens are a viable medium for studying economic contingencies in nonhumans. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2019 APA, all rights reserved)
we have shown that the generalized token functions like money in a token economy, and that it is possible to study token economics with nonhuman animals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
generalized tokens can be used to explore economic contingencies in nonhumans.
the token economy paradigm is well-suited to studying economic contingencies in nonhumans.

token production and exchange is a viable method for studying economic principles with nonhumans, including principles such as complementarity, substitutability, cross-price elasticity, and own-price elasticity.
